issues.legal_issue: A claim seeking relief expressly identified in an arbitration clause falls within the scope of that clause.
material_facts: All parties to the suit were parties to an agreement containing an arbitration clause.
The clause covered disputes about creation and enforcement of a charge over the flats, realization of sale proceeds, and continued occupation until specified dues were paid.
The suit sought enforcement of the mortgage, realization of the secured property, and vacant possession.
issues.conclusion: The subject matter of the suit fell within the scope of the arbitration agreement.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the judicial authority must determine whether the dispute is covered by the arbitration agreement. S.B.P. & Co. v. Patel Engineering Ltd. holds that the authority must decide whether the dispute is within the arbitration clause rather than refer the matter mechanically.

predicates.all_suit_parties_are_clause_parties: Every party to the suit is also a party to the agreement containing the arbitration clause.
predicates.claim_seeks_relief_described_in_arbitrat: The relief sought in the suit concerns matters the parties described in their arbitration clause.
predicates.suit_concerns_enforcement_of_security: The suit seeks enforcement of security over property and relief connected with that enforcement.

issues.definition: When all suit parties agreed to arbitrate and the suit seeks relief concerning enforcement of security that the clause describes, the claim falls within the clause.

issues.legal_issue: A reply opposing interim relief does not, by itself, amount to the first statement on the substance of the dispute for the purpose of seeking arbitration.
material_facts: The defendant filed a detailed affidavit opposing an application for interim relief.
The affidavit was filed before the written statement and addressed the interim application.
The defendant later applied for reference to arbitration without having filed a written statement.
issues.conclusion: The affidavit opposing interim relief did not amount to submission of the first statement on the substance of the dispute.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8(1) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 requires an application for reference before submission of the first statement on the substance of the dispute. Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd. v. Verma Transport Company explains that the inquiry is whether the party submitted to the court’s jurisdiction and waived arbitration; a response to an interim application does not necessarily do so. Food Corporation of India v. Yadav Engineer & Contractor supports distinguishing the main proceeding from supplemental proceedings.

predicates.arbitration_application_in_pending_suit: A defendant in a pending suit applies to have the dispute referred to arbitration.
predicates.defendant_reply_only_opposes_interim_rel: The defendant files a reply to resist interim relief rather than to submit the merits of the main dispute for adjudication.
predicates.no_written_statement_filed: The defendant has not filed a written statement in the suit when applying for arbitration.

issues.definition: In a pending suit, a defendant who has not filed a written statement does not submit the first merits statement merely by replying to oppose interim relief.

issues.legal_issue: Delay in applying for arbitration does not alone establish waiver when the defendant has contested supplemental proceedings and has not submitted the merits of the dispute to the court.
material_facts: The defendant opposed an application for interim relief and appointment of a receiver while that supplemental application remained pending.
Settlement discussions took place and did not result in a settlement.
The defendant applied for arbitration before filing a written statement or another statement on the substance of the dispute.
issues.conclusion: The application for arbitration was not barred merely because it was filed some time after the defendant entered appearance in the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 sets no separate time limit for an application, but requires it before the first statement on the substance of the dispute. Whether a party waived arbitration depends on its conduct; contesting supplemental proceedings and the passage of time alone do not establish submission to the court’s jurisdiction.

predicates.arbitration_application_in_pending_suit: A defendant in a pending suit applies to have the dispute referred to arbitration.
predicates.defendant_contests_only_supplemental_pro: The defendant contests interim or other supplemental proceedings without submitting the main dispute for adjudication.
predicates.settlement_discussions_fail: The parties pursue settlement discussions but do not reach a settlement.
predicates.no_merits_statement_precedes_arbitration: The defendant applies for arbitration before filing a statement submitting the substance of the main dispute to the court.

issues.definition: Where a defendant contests only supplemental proceedings and applies for arbitration before submitting the main dispute, failed settlement discussions and elapsed time alone do not bar the request.

issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking sale of mortgaged property to enforce a mortgage is not referable to arbitration because it requires adjudication by a public forum of rights that may affect persons beyond the arbitration parties.
material_facts: The suit sought enforcement of a mortgage by sale of the secured property and related relief.
The arbitration clause covered disputes concerning enforcement of a charge and realization of sale proceeds, and all suit parties were parties to the agreement.
Adjudication of the mortgage suit could affect other mortgagees, persons claiming a right of redemption or an interest in the property, and persons in possession or purchasing at sale.
issues.conclusion: The suit was for enforcement of a mortgage by sale and had to be tried by a court, not an arbitral tribunal; the application for reference to arbitration was therefore properly dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the court hearing the suit must decide arbitrability and refuse reference when the subject matter can be adjudicated only by a public forum. Sections 34(2)(b) and 48(2) recognize that a dispute may be incapable of settlement by arbitration. A mortgage is a transfer of a right in rem, and the Transfer of Property Act read with Order 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides for court adjudication of mortgage suits, including the interests of persons beyond the arbitration parties. Haryana Telecom Ltd. v. Sterlite Industries India Ltd. illustrates that a remedy reserved to a court cannot be referred to arbitration; Olympus Superstructures Pvt. Ltd. v. Meena Vijay Khetan distinguishes arbitrable contractual claims such as specific performance; Chiranjilal Shrilal Goenka v. Jasjit Singh addresses matters in rem; and Sukanya Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Jayesh H. Pandya rejects bifurcation of a suit for partial reference.

predicates.pending_suit_seeks_sale_of_mortgaged_pro: A suit pending before a court seeks sale of property to enforce a mortgage.
predicates.requested_decree_could_affect_nonparty_p: The requested decree could determine or affect property interests of persons beyond the parties to the arbitration agreement.

issues.definition: When a pending suit seeks sale of mortgaged property and its decree could affect nonparty property interests, the suit is not referable to arbitration.
